title: FarmHand rail-SCARA v1
subtitle: 37 parts · shown at 1:2 scale (viewer far-clip is 2 m) · tap a part

groups.frame: Frame + lift — bought extrusion, rails, screw

steps: Beam on the table front, X carriage on its wheels, X motor + belt.
Column on the X carriage, lead screw + Z motor at the bottom.
Z plate + nut, then the shoulder housing; press the two 6806s, J1 motor + intermediate shaft.
Spigot down through the bearings, clamp the 64T pulley under the deck; bolt the link to the root; J2 motor on top.
Elbow bearings, forearm spigot up through them; wrist motor underneath.
Wrist bearings and the quick-change flange.
Press the 3 balls, drop in the servo, offer the hand up to the flange (magnets pull it home).
MGN9 rail, carriages, jaws, TPU pads.
Clamp a shoe on every build plate.

parts.label: X rail beam
parts.note: 2040 V-slot, 1.5 m along the table front. The whole robot rides on it so it can park square in front of either printer — no long reach needed.

parts.label: X motor
parts.note: NEMA 17 + GT2 20T pulley. Belt moves the carriage; an AprilTag at each printer re-references X so belt stretch never adds up.

parts.label: X carriage
parts.note: Gantry plate on 4 V-wheels. The Z column bolts to it.

parts.label: Z column
parts.note: 2040 V-slot, 1 m tall. The only part of the robot that fights gravity is what slides up this.

parts.label: Lead screw T8×2
parts.note: 2 mm per turn = self-locking: thread friction beats the weight, so the arm cannot fall when power is cut. That is why there is no brake.

parts.label: Z motor
parts.note: NEMA 17 turning the lead screw. Needs only 36 % of its torque to lift the whole arm + 1.5 kg.

parts.label: Z motor mount
parts.note: Printed bracket, takes the screw thrust. Bolts to the column with M5 T-nuts.

parts.label: Brass nut
parts.note: Rides the lead screw; bolted to the Z plate so turning the screw lifts the carriage.

parts.label: Z carriage plate
parts.note: Bought gantry plate on V-wheels around the column. The shoulder housing bolts flat to it with 4 × M5.

parts.label: Shoulder housing
parts.note: Holds the two J1 bearings 60 mm apart — that spacing turns the arm's 14.4 N·m moment into ~240 N per bearing, easy for 6806s. Ribs carry it back to the plate.

parts.label: J1 motor
parts.note: NEMA 17 on the deck, shaft down. Two GT2 1:4 stages under the deck give 1:16 — 60 % of capacity for a 180° swing in 2.2 s.

parts.label: J1 bearing low
parts.note: 6806 (30×42×7) pressed in the bottom of the tower.

parts.label: J1 bearing top
parts.note: 6806 in the top of the tower. The upper-arm spigot runs through both.

parts.label: J1 intermediate
parts.note: 64T + 16T on an 8 mm shaft in two 608s: the middle of the 1:16 reduction.

parts.label: J1 output pulley
parts.note: 64T clamped on the bottom of the spigot (clamp hub, no set screw — set screws loosened on PAROL6).

parts.label: Upper arm — root
parts.note: J1 spigot + J2 motor seat + the first 1:4 stage. Hollow so cables go down the middle of J1.

parts.label: Upper arm — link
parts.note: Split at x = 120 so each half fits the H2S bed; 4 × M4 through the flanges. Open underside gets a snap-on cover over the belt.

parts.label: J2 motor
parts.note: Sits behind J1, not at the elbow, so J1 doesn't have to swing its mass at full reach.

parts.label: Elbow bearing top
parts.note: 6805. Forearm spigot runs up through both.

parts.label: Forearm
parts.note: Hangs under the upper arm so the hand reaches low into the printers. Belt to the wrist runs inside.

parts.label: Wrist motor
parts.note: NEMA 17 behind the elbow (balances the forearm), 1:4 belt to the wrist.

parts.label: Quick-change flange
parts.note: Three V-grooves underneath. Three steel balls on the hand drop into them: one exact position every time (~40 µm, Jubilee pattern). Magnets only pull it together; the balls carry the load.

parts.label: Steel ball
parts.note: Ø10 hardened ball, pressed into the hand. Sits 2.8 mm proud so the faces never touch — only the 6 ball/groove contacts do.

parts.label: Steel ball
parts.note: Kinematic coupling ball (2 of 3).

parts.label: Steel ball
parts.note: Kinematic coupling ball (3 of 3).

parts.label: Hand body
parts.note: Holds the gripper servo, jaw rail, the stylus barrel (right end) and the door hook (left end). Camera window on the side.

parts.label: Gripper servo
parts.note: Feetech STS3215. Reports its load, so the robot knows how hard it is squeezing.

parts.label: Jaw rail
parts.note: MGN9. Both jaws on one rail, driven opposite ways: the part always ends up centred.

parts.label: Jaw carriage
parts.note: MGN9 carriage, left jaw.

parts.label: Jaw carriage
parts.note: MGN9 carriage, right jaw.

parts.label: Jaw
parts.note: Rigid core + slot for a 2 mm steel 'nail' at the tip (fin-ray tips lose force on edges and thin plates).

parts.label: Jaw
parts.note: Same STL as the left jaw, turned 180°.

parts.label: Fin-ray pad
parts.note: TPU. Ribs fold toward the object when squeezed, so the pad wraps odd shapes instead of pushing them away.

parts.label: Plate shoe
parts.note: Clamps on the front notch of every build plate. The robot always grabs this tab, never the bare plate.
